title: Sunny and the Green Tree Frog

text: The warm rain stopped. The bush was cool and clean.
Sunny walked where every leaf hung bright with drops.
Beside a quiet pond she heard a sound,
a gentle “crrroak” from someone soft and near.
A plump green tree frog, smooth and shining wet,
with big gold eyes and a cream and cosy tummy.
He sat upon a broad and glossy leaf,
a single raindrop balanced on his nose.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What a happy song.”
“I love the quiet after rain,” he said.
He gave a little hop to another leaf,
and sent soft ripples spreading round the pond.
“It's cool and calm,” he murmured, blinking slow.
“The whole bush feels so fresh and clean and new.”
So Sunny watched the raindrops slip and drip,
and saw the round moon floating on the pond.
The tree frog gave a soft and sleepy croak,
a gentle song that drifted through the reeds.
He tucked beneath a leaf just like a roof,
and settled down all snug against the night.
Sunny found a bed of moss nearby,
still soft and cool and sweet from all the rain.
The pond was still. The frogs had hushed their song.
Everything was peaceful, cool, and calm.
Her eyes grew heavy as the last drops fell.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the sleeping frog,
dreaming to the drip-drip of the leaves.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little tree frog.
Goodnight, sleepy pond. Goodnight, little one.
